title: Budget unique backing allocations separately from logical payload
finding: RangeReader charges buffer.byteLength for each retained cache block. The synthetic probe confirms a one-byte view still costs a 1024-byte backing block and an external view survives cache eviction. Existing source-worker copying and bounded blocks do not establish the oversized long-lived packet-slab opportunity required to reopen R298.
novelty: R298 is the direct compaction owner; R047/R100 describe adjacent ownership costs, not a separate allocation-accounting win.
next_action: Keep the compaction stop. Reopen only with a real owner retaining small live slices after its siblings finish, then measure unique backing retention and copy cost; cache counters are not process memory.
reopen_condition: R298 was previously stopped under its scope. This does not reopen it without a changed retention workload and measurable benefit; retain only accounting regressions otherwise.

proposal_contract.Proposed mechanism: Track unique parent allocations and live views. Consider a bounded compaction copy only when retaining small survivors pins disproportionate storage; account for the copy and ownership transfer.
proposal_contract.Smallest useful experiment: Keep small packet slices from several large buffers while evicting prefixes; compare logical payload, unique backing bytes and actual retained allocator references before/after candidate compaction.
proposal_contract.Correctness gate: Identical packet bytes, valid sibling views, no stale pooled storage and no double release; memory counters distinguish proxies from actual owned allocations.
proposal_contract.Measure only after correctness: Owned allocation retention and copy cost separately; do not report view-byte reduction as freed browser process memory.
